nodes.label: Resilience to stuck TLS handshakes
nodes.rationale: One URLSession (DSNetwork), short attempt timeouts and jittered retries: any request when certainly not sent, idempotent ones also after timeouts/502-504; token refresh retried within the server 60 s grace window; WebSocket handshake timeout with quick reconnects; status stays syncing

nodes.label: Heartbeat: pong timeout replaces silently dead connections
nodes.norm_label: heartbeat: pong timeout replaces silently dead connections
nodes.rationale: Ping every 25 s, no pong in 10 s closes the socket, reconnect catches up from lastSeq; checkConnection() on foreground; reconnectNow cuts the backoff; before, a dead socket hung until app restart and remote edits never arrived (LiveSyncTests)

nodes.label: Live documents only for open notes
nodes.norm_label: live documents only for open notes
nodes.rationale: Closed documents stay in SQLite; their snapshots merge stored updates (CRDTUpdates.merge) without a document; close detaches before awaiting so a concurrent open gets a fresh instance; 10k notes: no growth on the iPad simulator vs +112 MB all live; Linux ~40 MB vs ~166 MB

nodes.label: Last keystrokes kept when the tab closes: docStore.persistUpdate merges updates arriving during a write into one row; on pagehide / tab hidden pending writes go synchronously to localStorage (ds.unsaved.<db>.<docId>), applied on next load once the doc is attached to sync (applyTail); removed with the account DB; e2e offline.spec.ts
nodes.norm_label: last keystrokes kept when the tab closes: docstore.persistupdate merges updates arriving during a write into one row; on pagehide / tab hidden pending writes go synchronously to localstorage (ds.unsaved.<db>.<docid>), applied on next load once the doc is attached to sync (applytail); removed with the account db; e2e offline.spec.ts
nodes.rationale: Found by folders.spec against the real server (title «В пап» instead of «В папку»): one IndexedDB row per keystroke lagged behind typing and the browser aborts uncommitted writes on unload, so the tail of the typed text was lost. localStorage is no more exposed than the updates already in IndexedDB.

nodes.label: wipeRevokedDevice() (auth/session.ts), run once even when REST and sync both signal: deletes the account DB (documents, outbox, notebook keys, attachment cache, ds.unsaved.* tails), session and recovery key, decrypted attachments in memory (forgetDecryptedAttachments), the tab's share keys
nodes.norm_label: wiperevokeddevice() (auth/session.ts), run once even when rest and sync both signal: deletes the account db (documents, outbox, notebook keys, attachment cache, ds.unsaved.* tails), session and recovery key, decrypted attachments in memory (forgetdecryptedattachments), the tab's share keys
nodes.rationale: REST and the sync socket can report the same revocation almost simultaneously; a single shared promise keeps the wipe idempotent.

nodes.label: D-53 on web: a disconnected device wipes its data — only on explicit device_revoked from the server (REST 401 { error: { code: "device_revoked", reason } } parsed by classifyApiFailure without a token refresh; sync error frame + close 4410 → SyncClient deviceRevoked, status revoked, no reconnect); any reason (user, password_change, recovery, token_reuse, account_deleted) wipes; plain 401 unauthorized and network errors keep the old keep-data sign-out
nodes.norm_label: d-53 on web: a disconnected device wipes its data — only on explicit device_revoked from the server (rest 401 { error: { code: "device_revoked", reason } } parsed by classifyapifailure without a token refresh; sync error frame + close 4410 → syncclient devicerevoked, status revoked, no reconnect); any reason (user, password_change, recovery, token_reuse, account_deleted) wipes; plain 401 unauthorized and network errors keep the old keep-data sign-out
nodes.rationale: Only the server can tell a revocation from a session that simply ended, so the wipe is bound to an explicit, unambiguous signal; an expired token, a proxy 401 or a network failure must never destroy local data.

nodes.label: Auth: Bearer accessToken 15 min + refreshToken 30 days rotated; reuse = theft → device revoked
nodes.community_name: Device revocation (2026-10-27): any request with a revoked device's access token and POST /auth/refresh with its refresh token → 401 { error: { code: "device_revoked", message, reason } }; only this code makes the client wipe local data; unknown/missing reason = user; 401 without such body (plain unauthorized, proxy page) → refresh or login only (classifyApiFailure, api/failures.json vectors)
nodes.norm_label: auth: bearer accesstoken 15 min + refreshtoken 30 days rotated; reuse = theft → device revoked

nodes.label: Device revocation (2026-10-27): any request with a revoked device's access token and POST /auth/refresh with its refresh token → 401 { error: { code: "device_revoked", message, reason } }; only this code makes the client wipe local data; unknown/missing reason = user; 401 without such body (plain unauthorized, proxy page) → refresh or login only (classifyApiFailure, api/failures.json vectors)
nodes.community_name: Device revocation (2026-10-27): any request with a revoked device's access token and POST /auth/refresh with its refresh token → 401 { error: { code: "device_revoked", message, reason } }; only this code makes the client wipe local data; unknown/missing reason = user; 401 without such body (plain unauthorized, proxy page) → refresh or login only (classifyApiFailure, api/failures.json vectors)
nodes.norm_label: device revocation (2026-10-27): any request with a revoked device's access token and post /auth/refresh with its refresh token → 401 { error: { code: "device_revoked", message, reason } }; only this code makes the client wipe local data; unknown/missing reason = user; 401 without such body (plain unauthorized, proxy page) → refresh or login only (classifyapifailure, api/failures.json vectors)
nodes.rationale: Clients must distinguish a deliberate disconnect (wipe, D-53) from an expired token or a network/proxy failure (retry, keep data). Old clients that do not know the code just see a 401, fail to refresh and ask to sign in again without wiping — a safe degradation.

nodes.label: device_revoked reason values: user (disconnected in devices list or logout), password_change, recovery (recovery key), token_reuse (used refresh token presented again), account_deleted (only with a still valid access token; afterwards /auth/refresh answers plain 401 unauthorized)
nodes.community_name: Device revocation (2026-10-27): any request with a revoked device's access token and POST /auth/refresh with its refresh token → 401 { error: { code: "device_revoked", message, reason } }; only this code makes the client wipe local data; unknown/missing reason = user; 401 without such body (plain unauthorized, proxy page) → refresh or login only (classifyApiFailure, api/failures.json vectors)
nodes.norm_label: device_revoked reason values: user (disconnected in devices list or logout), password_change, recovery (recovery key), token_reuse (used refresh token presented again), account_deleted (only with a still valid access token; afterwards /auth/refresh answers plain 401 unauthorized)

nodes.norm_label: refresh retry within 60 s returns same new refreshtoken (idempotent) while replacement unused

nodes.label: Device revocation in sync (2026-10-27): server sends error device_revoked with reason, then closes with code 4410 repeating reason; on hello with a revoked device's token no welcome; error frame always precedes the close; close without frame → reason from close reason, else user; client wipes local data, does not reconnect or send its queue
nodes.community_name: Device revocation (2026-10-27): any request with a revoked device's access token and POST /auth/refresh with its refresh token → 401 { error: { code: "device_revoked", message, reason } }; only this code makes the client wipe local data; unknown/missing reason = user; 401 without such body (plain unauthorized, proxy page) → refresh or login only (classifyApiFailure, api/failures.json vectors)
nodes.norm_label: device revocation in sync (2026-10-27): server sends error device_revoked with reason, then closes with code 4410 repeating reason; on hello with a revoked device's token no welcome; error frame always precedes the close; close without frame → reason from close reason, else user; client wipes local data, does not reconnect or send its queue
nodes.rationale: A distinct close code lets a client that lost the error frame still recognise revocation; old clients ignoring 4410 just reconnect, get refused again and end up asking to sign in without wiping (safe degradation).

nodes.label: 2026-10-27 server: revoked device gets unambiguous wipe signal — HTTP 401 device_revoked with reason (user, password_change, recovery, token_reuse) on any request and at token refresh, sync error device_revoked + close 4410 (also account_deleted); expired token stays plain 401 unauthorized; migration 0005 (devices.revoked_reason), contracts api.md and sync-protocol.md, test per reason
nodes.community_name: Device revocation (2026-10-27): any request with a revoked device's access token and POST /auth/refresh with its refresh token → 401 { error: { code: "device_revoked", message, reason } }; only this code makes the client wipe local data; unknown/missing reason = user; 401 without such body (plain unauthorized, proxy page) → refresh or login only (classifyApiFailure, api/failures.json vectors)
nodes.norm_label: 2026-10-27 server: revoked device gets unambiguous wipe signal — http 401 device_revoked with reason (user, password_change, recovery, token_reuse) on any request and at token refresh, sync error device_revoked + close 4410 (also account_deleted); expired token stays plain 401 unauthorized; migration 0005 (devices.revoked_reason), contracts api.md and sync-protocol.md, test per reason

nodes.label: Revoked device gets an unambiguous signal to wipe local data: HTTP 401 device_revoked with reason (user, password_change, recovery, token_reuse), sync error device_revoked + close 4410 (plus account_deleted when the account is deleted with an open connection); reason stored in devices.revoked_reason; expired token = plain 401 unauthorized, no wipe
nodes.community_name: Device revocation (2026-10-27): any request with a revoked device's access token and POST /auth/refresh with its refresh token → 401 { error: { code: "device_revoked", message, reason } }; only this code makes the client wipe local data; unknown/missing reason = user; 401 without such body (plain unauthorized, proxy page) → refresh or login only (classifyApiFailure, api/failures.json vectors)
nodes.norm_label: revoked device gets an unambiguous signal to wipe local data: http 401 device_revoked with reason (user, password_change, recovery, token_reuse), sync error device_revoked + close 4410 (plus account_deleted when the account is deleted with an open connection); reason stored in devices.revoked_reason; expired token = plain 401 unauthorized, no wipe
nodes.rationale: Refresh tokens of a revoked device are not deleted, so the device learns the reason even on its next token refresh; an expired token must never trigger a wipe.
